title: Do AI Labs Like Anthropic and OpenAI Have Economic Moats?
source_used: Morningstar (full text from the pre-fetched file)
key_facts: Morningstar is starting coverage of AI labs ahead of Anthropic's expected IPO; this is the first part of a three-part series on whether labs such as Anthropic and OpenAI have economic moats (lasting competitive advantages).
Morningstar is 'on the more bullish side': it thinks leading labs are building moats but does not view them as fully formed yet.
It sees two moat sources forming: a network effect from a data-and-product flywheel, and a structural cost advantage built on growing training costs and gigawatt-scale compute discounts.
Its core thesis is that inference demand (users generating code, text and answers) is scaling much faster than training and research costs, so long-term margins are driven by inference.
Initial margins are negative because training dominates; Morningstar says incremental margins are closer to 80%, the margin of pure inference.
Morningstar says Anthropic reached operating profitability in the first quarter of 2026, with 5% operating margins on $11 billion in quarterly sales, as its compute mix shifted toward inference.
If the labs cannot earn profits, the concern spreads to chips, power and data centers, whose spending commitments assume AI can be monetized at attractive returns.
quote_evidence: We’re on the more bullish side, as we think leading AI labs are building moats.
We do not view these moats as fully formed yet.
Anthropic reached operating profitability (not gross profitability, mind you) in the first quarter of 2026, posting 5% operating margins on $11 billion in quarterly sales.
why_it_matters_hint: Whether AI labs can earn lasting profits underpins the spending on chips, power and data centers and the expected Anthropic and OpenAI listings.
notes: Morningstar's own research view, not an independent finding; the figures on Anthropic are Morningstar's statement and are not attributed by the text to company filings. The text carries a standard disclosure that the authors own shares in securities mentioned.
